blacklistabilityReview.evidence: FreezeWatch re-review 2026-10-19. Materiality: the census supply split is Ethereum 90.3142%, Polygon 9.6858%; on-chain totals at Ethereum block 26224775 (541,238.050674 WUSD) and Polygon block 95790212 (58,045.600231 WUSD) reproduce 9.69%, so Polygon is sub-threshold and does not set the verdict. Ethereum WUSD 0x7cd017ca5ddb86861fa983a34b5f495c6f898c41 is an ERC1967 proxy (implementation slot 0x3ac7b6769c5e4a5c17986bd39d9d8b2e9e09227e, Fireblocks ERC20F). At block 26224775 paused()=false and accessRegistry()=0x0. Verified source gates transfer and transferFrom through _requireHasAccess, which is a no-op while the registry is unset; accessRegistryUpdate(address) is callable by CONTRACT_ADMIN_ROLE (0x26bc37aacc94a56d5b2a641c59a6f7f8880eb3df active), after which any account absent from the registry is rejected as sender or receiver and recoverTokens(address,uint256) by RECOVERY_ROLE (0x36c6d0386c44bb7e95a564ff6d4309d2f6381fee active) can move a de-listed holder's balance to the caller. Transfers are also globally pausable (PAUSER_ROLE 0xa2faa105883af5cbef6f95826db420e5ab5594fc active) and the implementation is UUPS-upgradeable (DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE 0x731efdc933464ed81bf3ea961e9fdadc62e83bd1 can grant UPGRADER_ROLE). No holder is currently denied and no blacklist/freeze mapping exists, so the posture is a mutable holder-facing control surface rather than an active holder-targeted control: reviewedStatus is possible. Role grants occurred at blocks 21390703 and 21390890 with no RoleRevoked events.

bridgeRouteRisk.summary: WUSD is issuer-minted natively by WSPN on all three tracked networks. Each deployment is an ERC1967 proxy over an AccessControl ERC20 (ERC20F family) whose complete RoleGranted history shows mint rights only with WSPN operator accounts: the same DEFAULT_ADMIN EOA 0x731efdc9 and minter EOA 0x1a41b592 on every chain, plus chain-local mint/burn operator contracts. masterMinter() and LayerZero endpoint() probes revert and no third-party bridge contract holds MINTER_ROLE, so the earlier LayerZero external lock/mint candidate is not supported by on-chain evidence; cross-chain movement is issuer-native burn/mint through WSPN rails.
